And Babylon the great came into memorie before God, ∷ {{outside R|∷ The citie or commonvvealth of the vvicked deuided into three partes: into infidels, Heretikes, and euil Catholikes. This citie is here called Babylon, vvhereof {{ls}}ee the Annotat. vpon the next chapter ''v. 5''. · Ier. 25, 15.}} to giue her the cuppe of vvine of the indignation of his vvrath. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=20|align=float}}† And euery Iland fled, and mountaines vvere not found. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=21|align=float}}† And great haile like a talent came downe from heauen vpon men: and men bla{{ls}}phemed God for the plague of the haile: becau{{ls}}e it vvas made exceding great.

{{c|''The harlot Babylon clothed vvith diuers ornaments, 6 and drunken of the bloud of Martyrs, {{ls}}itteth vpon a bea{{ls}}t that hath {{ls}}euen heades and ten hornes: 7 al which things the Angel expoundeth.''}}

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=1|align=float}}{{dropinitial|A}}{{sc|Nd}} there came one of the {{ls}}euen Angels vvhich had the {{ls}}euen vials, & {{ls}}pake vvith me, {{ls}}aying, Come, I vvil {{ls}}hevv thee ∷ {{outside R|∷ The final damnation of the vvhole companie of the reprobate, called here the great vvhore.}} the damnation of the great harlot, vvhich {{ls}}itteth vpon c ∷ {{outside R|∷ c The{{ls}}e many vvaters are many peoples. ''v. 15''.}} many vvaters, {{verse|chapter=17|verse=2|align=float}}† vvith vvhom the kings of the earth haue fornicated, and they vvhich inhabite the earth haue been drunke of the vvine of her vvhoredom. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=3|align=float}}† And he tooke me avvay in {{ls}}pirit into the de{{ls}}ert. And I {{ls}}avv a vvomā {{ls}}itting vpon a {{ls}}carlet coloured bea{{ls}}t, ful of names of bla{{ls}}phemie, hauing {{ls}}euen heades, and ten hornes. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=4|align=float}}† And the vvoman vvas clothed round about vvith purple and {{ls}}carlet, and gilted vvith gold, and pretious {{ls}}tone, and pearles, hauing a golden cup in her hand, ful of the abomination & filthines of her fornication. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=5|align=float}}† And in her forehead a name vvritten, ''{{sup|‖}} My{{ls}}terie'': {{sup|‖}} Babylon the great, mother of the fornications and the abominations of the earth. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=6|align=float}}† And I {{ls}}avv the vvoman {{sup|‖}} drunken of the bloud of the Sainctes, and of the bloud of the martyrs of {{sc|Iesvs}}. And I marueled vvhen I had {{ls}}een her, vvith great admiration. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=7|align=float}}† And the Angel {{ls}}aid to me, Vvhy doe{{ls}}t thou maruel? I vvil tel thee the my{{ls}}terie of the woman, and of the bea{{ls}}t that carieth her, which hath the {{ls}}euen heades and the ten hornes.
